description: Regional bundle of a world bundle's window at a whole-number scale (world_pipeline region, erosion plan Phase E): the global base elevation upsampled with band-limited noise and carved by the analytical stream-power relief on channels pinned to the global rivers; sea, lakes, rivers, January and July temperature and precipitation, the climate class and present-day ice on the fine grid. The run takes the world bundle, the window (--window degrees or --pixels global cells) and the scale (--scale) as native options or from the registered arguments; its seed and grid come from the world bundle, so the grid is the window's, not W x W/2. Judged by the user's review; checks guard the window block, the fields and their ranges. Two windows are compared on their overlap with scripts/evaluation/regional_overlap.py. A refinement hierarchy bundle (--scale a power of landscape.refinement.factor, multiscale plan S2.3) is checked level by level from its diagnostics (parent-mean-exact; border-step reports each level's 99th-percentile step across parent edges against 50 m, S2.7) and, given a coarser bundle of the same world with evaluate --coarser BUNDLE, against it (level-consistency; resolution-invariance reports the land's hypsometry and channel share of both); a single pass reports them as not applicable. anisotropy reports the land's slope-spectrum anisotropy (crests SW-NE over NW-SE, E-W over N-S) overall and around each level's parent period, with the parent lattice's peak (S3.7: the striping measured independently of the hillshade's light; relief-ne and relief-sw light the map from the other diagonals).

targets.step: S3.4 (the plan's target is lake (169, 60); this is every lake of the kept box)

maps.name: terrain
maps.title: Regional terrain: elevation (m relative to sea level) with sea, ice, lakes and the rivers of an annual flow of at least 150 (legacy units, the legacy map's default)

maps.name: relief
maps.title: Regional relief: the terrain map times a hillshade (light from the north-west, 45 degrees up; vertical exaggeration 10, so 300 m of relief shows at 10 km pixels)

maps.name: relief-ne
maps.title: Regional relief lit from the north-east (azimuth 45 degrees, 45 degrees up; vertical exaggeration 10): beside the north-west light, it tells the terrain's striping from the light's

maps.name: relief-sw
maps.title: Regional relief lit from the south-west (azimuth 225 degrees, 45 degrees up; vertical exaggeration 10): the north-east light's opposite, so ridges swap their lit and dark sides

maps.name: terrain-fade
maps.title: Regional terrain with rivers fading in with their flow (legacy river colour)

maps.name: discharge
maps.title: Discharge (log10 m3/s; dark: none, sea, lakes)

maps.name: lakes
maps.title: Lake surface elevation (m above sea level; dark where there is no lake)

maps.name: ice-thickness
maps.title: Present-day ice thickness (m; dark where there is none)

preferred.why: the user (2026-10-11): window A is read against the Himalaya and the southern Tibetan plateau, not the nearest-latitude arc

earth.note: Earth reference windows (multiscale plan S1.2, scripts/evaluation/earth_windows.py): an ETOPO 2022 window at the map's pixel count and metres per pixel beside the terrain and relief maps, kind earth; --earth NAME on evaluate chooses the catalogue entry, otherwise the preferred entry for the window block (preferred: pixels c0,r0,c1,r1 as the run's --pixels, entry), otherwise the entry whose metres_per_pixel range holds the map's and whose centre latitude is nearest the window's.

review_status: Draft written by an agent on 2026-10-08 (erosion plan, step E2d). The user rewrites it; until then a verdict on it is a reading aid, not a judgement of the map.

review.question: Is the regional map the global map zoomed in: the same coasts, ranges, rivers and lakes, with detail added and none contradicted?
review.good: every global coast, range, river and lake in its place; detail inside global cells, not new features at the global scale

review.question: Is the map free of the global grid: no blocks, steps or straight edges at the size of a global cell?
review.good: relief, coasts and climate vary smoothly across global cell edges; no checkerboard and no squares of one value

review.question: Do the rivers run downhill in valleys to the sea or a lake, gaining discharge?
review.good: connected channels in valleys that end at a coast or a lake; no channel that stops on dry land or climbs a slope
